finite_default_domain.definition: All 49 blank rectangular input sizes with independent width and height 3 through 9.
finite_default_domain.scope: Default native parameter distribution only; finite input count is not inflated by repeated sampling.

provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The mechanism paints a one-cell-wide frame along all four borders of the grid and leaves the interior as it is in the input. Under the D4 transforms, the set of border cells maps onto itself. A rotation or reflection only swaps which dimension is rows and which is columns, and the emitted program reads the actual visible shape. So the edge-painting needs no direction-specific rewrite. The program paints the first and last rows and the first and last columns in visible coordinates, on rectangular grids of any shape. The only colour role is the frame colour, original 8 (cyan). The factory specializes it as palette[8]. Interior cells are copied from the input, so the background (palette[0]) is kept without being named.
draft_notes.limitations: The frame colour is a constant taken from palette[8]. It is not inferred from the demonstrations, which matches the constructor: it always uses cyan. The constructor's domain is all-background grids of 3..9 by 3..9, so its interior content is always background. The program copies the interior unchanged and does not force it to the background colour. Neither the generator nor the fixtures show any defects, ties, or contradictions. The emitted program degrades gracefully on 1-wide grids, where the whole grid becomes frame, although those lie outside the constructor's domain. No tests were run.
